subject: Intermittent embeddings failures impacting GreenLedger — SLA claim & evidence request
messages:
From: Samantha Ellis <samantha@greenledger.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@greenledger.com
Date: 2028-08-14 09:12 PDT
Subject: Repeated 503s to embeddings endpoint — production impact

Hi Aditya,

We started seeing a spike of 503s hitting Redwood's embeddings endpoint around 08:40 PDT this morning. The error rate climbed from <0.1% to ~9% for roughly 25 minutes before falling back around 09:05. This impacted several batch jobs (we had to restart two pipelines).

Can you please:
- Confirm whether the event qualifies as an SLA incident (we're on a paid plan and need to understand credit eligibility)
- Pull logs for the 08:35–09:10 window and share them (or tell us how to fetch them)
- Provide an ETA for a postmortem and any interim mitigation steps you recommend

Example request IDs we saw: req_3f8a9b, req_3f8b1c, req_3f8d33.

This is causing revenue impact for us — would like an expedited review.

Thanks,
Samantha Ellis
Head of Data Platform
GreenLedger

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Samantha Ellis <samantha@greenledger.com>
Date: 2028-08-15 08:15 PDT
Subject: Re: Repeated 503s to embeddings endpoint — production impact

Aditya / Marissa / Samantha — I pulled the runbook-level telemetry and a request-level sample for the 08:30–09:10 PDT window. Summary:

- Peak error window: 2028-08-14 08:41:20–2028-08-14 09:04:55 PDT (approx 23m 35s)
- Root cause (initial): transient upstream load shedding on a single availability set during a bursty inbound pattern; KV-cache thrashing on a subset of nodes caused short-lived request routing failures (503s).
- Impacted surface: embeddings.batch and embeddings.embed single-shot calls — downstream retries increased queue pressure.

I've attached a sanitized log bundle (greenledger_log_bundle_0814.zip) and internal SRE notes (sre_rca_notes.txt). The bundle contains per-request traces for the sample IDs you provided and aggregated error-rate graphs.

Preliminary assessment for SLA: the event is an availability degradation that meets the "service interruption" window for the embeddings product per our public SLA. Final eligibility and credit amount requires mapping your billed usage for that window (Marissa: can you pull the daily usage breakdown to feed the credit calc?).

Interim mitigations applied the same morning: failed node removed from rotation and cache tuning rolled to the pool; we also adjusted burst-protection thresholds. We'll follow with a full postmortem.

Let me know if Samantha needs any additional artifacts or a redacted raw trace.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: greenledger_log_bundle_0814.zip, sre_rca_notes.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-16 15:04 PDT
Subject: Re: Intermittent embeddings failures impacting GreenLedger — SLA credit & postmortem timeline

Hi Samantha — following Grace's analysis, we ran your usage through the credit model. Attached is an initial worksheet (slo_calc_worksheet.xlsx) that outlines the calculation steps:

- Confirmed affected window: 2028-08-14 08:41:20–2028-08-14 09:04:55 PDT (23m 35s)
- Measured impact: approx 9% error-rate delta during the window across three API keys
- Preliminary credit estimate: prorated credit equivalent to 0.45 days of usage on your monthly plan, applied as a billing credit (final number to be reconciled against invoice records).

Next steps:
1) We will finalize the postmortem doc and publish a redacted version within 5 business days (internal RCA will include deeper telemetry).
2) Credit will be applied to your next billing cycle pending final reconciliation.
3) If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min call this week to walk through the RCAs and mitigations — propose Thursday 10:00 PDT.

Please confirm whether the provisional credit approach is acceptable or if finance needs a different path.

Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate the expedited report and the sample IDs; they helped accelerate the investigation.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
